claims.statement: Kafka sink remains Experimental with Connector runtime reachability; public KafkaViewSink supports row export but SQL CREATE SINK does not configure it.
The legacy SinkConnector pre_commit interface stages only epoch/count markers, whereas pre_commit_payload retains a complete row envelope for recovery.
KafkaViewSink is explicitly attached to a connected KafkaSink, ShardDb, view operator ID and column count; deliver_next drains pending or new work and returns false when no further logged rows exist.

Safe view export requires one owner, a dedicated topic/connector identity, a retained append-only monotonically committed view log and fixed schema; progress rejects changed view ID, column count or topic but does not fingerprint the full schema.
The CLI retains stale row-export-unsupported guidance in its removed cold-tier configuration error and corresponding regression assertion despite current runtime row export.

KafkaViewSink first materializes a snapshot, rejects negative snapshot multiplicities, and then exports signed rows for one nonempty view epoch strictly after the saved cursor; even an empty view receives a snapshot envelope.

The v1 row envelope separates sink transaction epoch from view_epoch and carries typed values and signed weights; floats use hexadecimal bit representations and whole-row weight summation reconstructs the relation rather than primary-key upserts.

Each view envelope is one transaction record on partition zero keyed by the decimal sink epoch, providing an atomic snapshot-before-changes stream to read_committed consumers, not exactly-once arbitrary downstream side effects.

KafkaViewSink flushes the full pending payload, target identity, snapshot status, view cursor and next transaction sequence under its connector-specific kafka-view key before broker commit, then clears pending and flushes again; pending work blocks another stage.

The generic sink contract requires durable staging with the shard epoch batch before cluster-checkpoint-gated external commit; Kafka commit asserts the checkpoint horizon and absence of prior delivery, so uncertain commits must use recovery instead of blind commit retries.

KafkaViewSink does not wait for CheckpointCoordinator: it sets the sink horizon after flushing its own pending progress, whereas the cluster coordinator independently collects shard confirmations and commits the cluster manifest.

Kafka recovery requires reconnecting with the same transactional identity to fence old transactions; connect configures rockstream-{connector_id}-{topic}, idempotence and acks=all and initializes transactions.

CheckBeforeCommit row recovery validates pending target identity and envelope, skips publication for an exact existing payload, fails on conflicting bytes, and republishes the saved payload in a new transaction only after confirmed absence.

Delivery lookup scans all partitions from the beginning with read_committed, compares stable offsets to read_uncommitted high watermarks, and confirms absence only after EOF on all initially stable partitions; setup, polling and five-second timeout failures remain DeliveryUnknown rather than triggering publication.

Lookup accepts connector-less legacy markers as epoch candidates, but exact row recovery rejects mismatching marker bytes; safe deduplication consequently depends on isolated ownership, effective fencing and retained delivery records, not just epoch equality.
View export fails closed above a 900 KiB envelope or 64 MiB view-log read; chunked delivery and automatic log compaction are outside the adapter, and oversize envelopes do not advance saved progress.

Kafka staging admission is bounded at five staged epochs with a count accessor and backpressure predicate; duplicate staging or overflow fails, while KafkaViewSink permits only one durable pending transaction.

Kafka errors distinguish pre-commit RS-4003, commit RS-4004, I/O RS-4002 and unknown delivery RS-4030; initialization/commit have 15-second timeouts and abort/offset attachment ten seconds, while simulated transaction timeout preserves recovery semantics rather than proving production latency.

Secret rotation enforces name binding and queues a token applied at staging/commit boundaries, updating token ID and counters, but does not reconfigure Kafka producer credentials; zero restart/failed-batch accessors do not establish broker authentication success.
KafkaSink offers transactional source-offset attachment requiring consumer group metadata, but KafkaViewSink does not use it, so durable view cursors are not atomic Kafka source-offset commits.

The real Kafka view-delivery test compares exact typed consumer streams and final relations across uninterrupted operation, staging crashes for snapshot/update/delete and broker commit before final cursor save; it includes negative controls, empty snapshots, oversize rejection and identity/payload conflicts.

Marker guarantee-matrix tests have narrower transport/recovery scope than typed row-delivery tests, and the surface contract explicitly preserves Experimental status without an overall qualification proof.

The M3 model reasons about checkpoint-coupled 2PC and profile-dispatched recovery with bounded epochs and crashes, not external Kafka retention, authentication or downstream consumer correctness; exactly-once row delivery remains scoped to tested behavior and external ownership/storage/Kafka assumptions.
